definition: The task of assigning predefined categories or labels to a piece of text.
details: Text classification underlies many practical NLP applications, including spam detection, topic categorization, and content moderation, and can be tackled with anything from simple classical ML models to fine-tuned transformer models.

explainer.lead: Text classification assigns predefined categories or labels to a piece of text. It matters because it underlies practical applications like spam detection, topic categorization, and content moderation.

tiers.eli5: It is like sorting mail into labeled bins, where each message gets dropped into the bin it belongs to.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers tackle it with anything from simple classical ML models to fine-tuned transformer models, matching method to label complexity and data size. The pitfall is choosing an overkill model when simple classical methods suffice.
tiers.paperLevel: The task of assigning predefined categories or labels to a piece of text; approaches range from classical ML models to fine-tuned transformers.

explainer.example: A message arriving in an inbox is labeled spam or not spam before the user sees it.
